subject.declared_domain: The MDPF delivery-cadence contract that D3's seed names as 'a WRITTEN D3 instance' and parenthesises as 'T-1 by 02:00Z'. This card covers that contract AS AN ARTIFACT: whether it is written, where, what it actually says, and how it fails. It does NOT card the D3 rail (wave 1, SC-g-*), the estate-contracts store as a whole (W2-qgtd covers its sibling carrier), or the MDPF pipeline's operational health.

methodology.how: MDPF's delivery-cadence obligations are DECLARED, not derived: they are hand-authored contract_records in the estate-contracts store, written by an AE seat and loaded in-VPC. Three of the seven MDPF records carry a delivery_cadence obligation -- two process records (mdpf-daily-trigger, mdpf-daily-runner) and one artifact record (aggregate_aua_timeseries.json). The obligation is a TYPE reference into D3's obligation_types; the actual cadence value is a free-text string on the optional `cadence` field. It COMPOSES D3's obligation_types vocabulary and the contract_record shape; it INVENTS the per-subject MDPF cadence declarations themselves. ⛔ NOTHING GENERATES OR CHECKS THESE -- the store's own README states it fires nothing, renders records, and runs no scan and no schedule.

declared_opinions: ⛔ EVENT-ONLY AS A DECLARED CADENCE: the one MDPF record carrying a cadence VALUE declares it as 'event-only: S3 ObjectCreated on the INF spine completion marker; no schedule of its own'. Treating a dependency on another pipeline's completion marker AS the cadence -- rather than as an accelerator alongside one -- is a declared position, stated plainly in the record.

OBLIGATION WITHOUT VALUE: two of the three records declaring delivery_cadence carry no cadence value at all. That the obligation TYPE can be asserted without the value that would make it checkable is permitted by the contract_record shape, and MDPF exercises that permission twice.

PROCESS AND ARTIFACT RECORDS SHARE ONE OBLIGATION VOCABULARY: mdpf-daily-trigger (a process) and aggregate_aua_timeseries.json (an artifact) both carry delivery_cadence, so the obligation is asserted at two different grains in one file.

key.key_expression: The YAML mapping key under `contracts:` in org/modules/graph/estate-contracts/mdpf.contracts.yaml, taken VERBATIM. Grammar `<grain>:<identifier>` over two grains: `process:<slug>` for the three process records, `artifact:<s3-uri>` for the four artifact records. Compute: parse the YAML with contract_declare_lint.py's own find_records predicate (never a grep) and read the key -- no derivation. ⛔ THE EXPRESSION YIELDS MORE THAN THIS ROW'S identity_space NAMES, AND THE GAP IS THE POINT: the artifact half's key is the FULL s3:// URI, not the basename the identity_space lists, and three of the four artifact keys carry `{date}` / `{firmId}` / `{artifact}` placeholders -- so those keys are PATTERNS matching a SET, and no expression resolves them to one member without a date and a firm.
key.evidence:
⛔ THE SUBJECT AS NAMED DOES NOT RESOLVE TO THE SUBJECT AS WRITTEN, AND THAT IS THIS CARD'S KEY FINDING. D3's seed names 'the MDPF delivery-cadence contract (T-1 by 02:00Z)' -- one contract, one time-based commitment. What is written is THREE records across two grains, of which one carries a cadence value, and that value is 'event-only: S3 ObjectCreated on the INF spine completion marker; no schedule of its own' -- not a T-1 time commitment at all. The seed's name and the store's content are two id spaces with nothing declaring the mapping: no record cites the seed, and the seed cites no record. crosses_spaces is measured TRUE on that basis, and on a second crossing measured within the file -- process ids and artifact filenames are two key grammars in one obligation vocabulary, and two of the artifact keys are TEMPLATES ({date}.json) rather than identifiers, so they cannot be joined to a concrete object without expansion. key_is_stable is 'unknown' with basis ABSENT: templated keys are stable as templates and unresolvable as instances, and I did not establish which a consumer is expected to match on.

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: SILENT AND WELL-FORMED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. A consumer asking this contract for MDPF's delivery cadence gets: for two of three records, an obligation with no value -- a declared duty and nothing to check it against; for the third, a cadence string that names another pipeline's event rather than a time. Neither returns an error, and 'no cadence declared' is indistinguishable from 'cadence not yet authored'.
silent_degrade_paths: two of three delivery_cadence records carry no cadence value, so an obligation is asserted with nothing that could fail -- the contract_record shape permits it and no lint objects

⛔ the one declared cadence is 'event-only ... no schedule of its own', which is the shape CLAUDE.md's own standing rule names as a defect -- a pipeline whose only trigger is another pipeline's success freezes silently when its upstream breaks. THE RECORD DECLARES THIS PLAINLY AND HONESTLY; I am recording that the declaration matches a named defect pattern, and per QUALIFY-DO-NOT-FIX and W2-m-3 I am NOT ruling on whether it should change.

the seed characterises the contract as 'T-1 by 02:00Z' while the located records say otherwise, so a consumer reading the rule bank and a consumer reading the store get different cadences for the same subject, both confidently
two record keys are templates ({date}.json, {date}.parquet); a consumer joining on them literally matches nothing and gets a clean zero

verdict.why: The contract IS written -- three MDPF records declare a delivery_cadence obligation in a file that exists, parses and validates -- so the seed's claim that a written D3 instance exists is substantially true, and I nearly carded the opposite before widening. QUALIFIED rather than SOUND on four bounded defects: (1) the seed names it 'T-1 by 02:00Z' and no artifact I opened carries that formulation, while the one record with a cadence value declares something materially different; (2) two of three records assert the obligation with no value, so a duty is declared that nothing can check; (3) the declared cadence is event-only with no schedule of its own, which is the exact shape the estate's own standing rule names as freezing silently when upstream breaks -- declared honestly by the record, recorded here, NOT ruled on; (4) two record keys are templates that join to nothing literally. Not UNSOUND: the declarations are real, honest and readable, and a consumer who reads the store rather than the seed gets accurate information. NOT INCOMPLETE: all 7 rows are worked. Two scalars sit below measured -- cadence at 'inferred' because I deliberately did not measure the APPLIED delivery state, and key at 'absent' on unresolved template-vs-instance matching. ⛔ MY ABSENCE CLAIM IS BOUNDED: I opened three artifacts of twenty-six MDPF-named candidates, and the T-1 formulation could live in one of the twenty-three I did not open. ⛔ NO FORWARD DISPOSITION per W2-m-3: omitted, and nothing here is an opinion on this contract's future -- including the event-only cadence, which I have described and not judged. Per QUALIFY-DO-NOT-FIX this lane remediated nothing.
